Subject: ISV onboarding: Redwood listing & SOC2 / contract questions

Hi Aisha,

Thanks for taking this — excited to get Redwood into the PlatformWorks partner catalog. A couple of items we need to unblock on our end before we can schedule engineering work:

- SOC2 report (or SOC2 in-scope evidence) and vendor security questionnaire
- Confirmation of supported integration patterns (marketplace listing + hosted integration vs. private customer-managed option)
- Draft MSA / partner terms so our legal team can review redlines
- A suggested timeline for marketplace onboarding and any gating criteria (entitlements, technical checklist)

We'd like to aim for a soft listing in Q3 if the legal/security checks are straightforward. Can you share the SOC2 and a contact on your side for legal + tech? I’ve attached a first-pass integration spec and our MSA redlines for context.

Appreciate it — happy to hop on a call this week if useful.

Best,
Shannon Park
Head of Partnerships, PlatformWorks
shannon@platformworks.com

2) Security artifacts: if you can send the vendor questionnaire and the latest SOC2 report (or SOC2 bridge letter) we’ll get it to InfoSec.

4) Timeline: Shannon, what internal stakeholders/timezones do we coordinate with for a technical kickoff?

Proposed next steps:
- PlatformWorks to share vendor questionnaire + clarify DPA requirement (action: Shannon)
- Redwood to provide our marketplace integration checklist + staging access timeline (action: Laura/Karthik)
- Legal to review MSA redlines (action: Markus)

Can we schedule a 30-minute kickoff Wed or Thu (PDT)?

Thanks — Aisha

Hi Shannon / Aisha — quick product/roadmap clarifications so we scope the integration correctly:

1) Integration patterns we support today:
   - Marketplace listing -> redirect to hosted Redwood API (recommended for fastest onboarding)
   - Marketplace listing -> private deployment reference (customer-managed, requires dedicated onboarding and additional entitlements)
   - Direct API integration for ISV-managed workflows (requires API key exchange + DPA)

2) Questions for PlatformWorks (please answer in reply):
   - Which integration pattern are you targeting for initial listing? (redirect hosted / private reference / direct API)
   - Expected monthly active customers routed from PlatformWorks to Redwood (ballpark) and peak qps per customer
   - Do you require model pinning or dedicated instance options at launch?
   - Any SSO/SCIM requirements for publisher admin flows?

3) Dependencies & gating for a marketplace listing:
   - Completed security review (SOC2 + questionnaire)
   - Product checklist completed (I’ve attached our checklist)
   - Billing entitlements set up with partner ops (we’ll need CloudHub contact looped)

If you can provide the answers above and a contact for a staging AWS account or test tenancy, we can aim to surface the first checklist pass in 7–10 business days.

Attachments: redwood-marketplace-integration-checklist.xlsx

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Product Manager, Marketplace Integrations | Redwood Inference

Hi Shannon — quick technical notes / asks before the kickoff:

- Can you share the current API schema for the PlatformWorks side (auth, callback URLs, expected headers)?
- For hosted integration: do you expect synchronous generation calls in-path, or an evented callback model? Typical latency SLOs?
- Do you plan to send user prompts that require long context windows (>8k tokens) or short chat-style interactions? This affects our instance selection and KV cache expectations.
- If you want private deployment references, we’ll need a list of sample customer sizes and any compliance constraints (data residency).

Proposed tech kickoff: Thu 22 May 2025 10:00 PDT — we’ll provision a staging API key and a small test workload. If that works, I’ll send calendar invite+pre-reqs (postman collection, schema examples).

Thanks — Karthik
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: markus_klein@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: ISV onboarding: Redwood listing & SOC2 / contract questions

Hi Shannon — a couple of legal items to accelerate review:

1) Path options for contracting:
   A) Marketplace-native flow: publisher agreement + marketplace DPA. Faster for listing, Redwood would rely on marketplace entitlements for billing and support scopes.
   B) Direct publisher MSA: Redwood signs a standalone MSA with PlatformWorks (allows more control over support SLAs and entitlements but takes longer).

2) Immediate asks:
   - Please provide the vendor security questionnaire and SOC2 (or SSAE bridge) so InfoSec can triage.
   - Confirm whether PlatformWorks requires vendor indemnity or special export controls.
   - Provide the contact at CloudHub partner ops (cc’d) who will own entitlement provisioning — we’ll coordinate billing and publisher metadata with them.

I’ve attached a short legal checklist with typical redlines to expect. If PlatformWorks prefers route A, we can target a trimmed review (2–3 weeks); route B will likely be 6+ weeks depending on negotiation.

Suggested next steps: Shannon to share questionnaires + confirm preferred contracting path; Markus to confirm Redwood redlines within 48 hours of receiving PlatformWorks MSA.

Regards,
Markus Klein
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: legal-ask-checklist.txt
